problem: Navigation instructions are still evaluated with reference-based n-gram metrics (BLEU, ROUGE) that miss functional navigability. Agent-based evaluation needs costly, licensed visual simulators (Google Street View, Matterport3D), and perception errors confound linguistic quality.
motivation: Instruction quality should be judged by whether a rational agent can follow it, not by lexical overlap. Map2Seq provides aligned OpenStreetMap data, so visual recognition can be removed from the loop. Symbolic map reasoning gives a cheap, reproducible, interpretable evaluator.
key_idea: Use a training-free hierarchical LLM agent (sub-instruction planner plus topological-graph navigator over JSON-serialized OSM data) as the judge, and take its execution success and trajectory fidelity as proxy scores for instruction navigability.
insight: Representation format matters a lot. Structured JSON and textual encodings reach about 63% and 61% SR, while Graphviz gets 40% and the ASCII grid only 10%, because the LLM struggles with pixel-like text layouts. An LLM sub-goal divider beats both feeding the full instruction and rule-based splitting on periods, and it helps most on hard instructions (SR 53.8% vs 23.1% and 38.5%). Error-driven prompt fixes (iteration counters for counting, POI clarifications, dropping lat/lng) give large further gains. Higher thinking levels help mainly on hard instructions but cost many more tokens.
method: Visible Area Construction: from the current node and heading, follow the street forward (min heading difference, under 100°) until u intersections (degree>2) are passed, plus 3 lookahead nodes, to simulate a human's limited view.
Sub-instruction Agent: an LLM parses the instruction into atomic sub-goals (MOVE_FORWARD, TURN_LEFT, TURN_RIGHT) with TODO/IN_PROGRESS/COMPLETED status and extracts landmarks by OSM category.

Landmark grounding and POI proximity: RapidFuzz partial_ratio matches landmarks to POI tags; POIs within 50 m of path nodes get a Haversine distance and a Forward/Left/Right/Back direction relative to heading, with letter IDs.

Navigator Agent: given the sub-goal, its status and iteration count, the position, the heading and the JSON local graph, the LLM outputs a status and the next node ID. It stops when all sub-goals are done, at 100 steps, or after 15 retries on one sub-goal.

Spatial representations compared: textual incident encoding, structured JSON, Graphviz-style, and a BFS grid/matrix. JSON was optimized by adding POI criteria, iteration counters and removing lat/lng.
Agent-as-Judge meta-evaluation: NE, SR, OSR, SDTW and nDTW are correlated with binary human navigability ratings on 100 instructions.

setting.backbone: Gemini-3 Pro (frozen, default temperature 1.0, high thinking by default)
setting.observation: symbolic OSM local graph (nodes, edges, headings, POIs) serialized as JSON; no vision
setting.action_space: discrete next-waypoint node selection on OSM topological graph, with sub-goal status
setting.simulator: none (OSM graph from Map2Seq; no visual simulator)
setting.privileged: OSM map graph and POI tags of the environment; start node and initial heading; no GT path at test time

numbers_note: Map2Seq is not a canonical benchmark name, so it is labeled 'other:Map2Seq'. The paper's split labels (Test_Seen/Test_Unseen) are mapped to test-seen/test-unseen. The ablation subset is described as 'seen validation' in one place and Test_Seen in another. The abstract's 68.5% NE reduction claim is not directly verifiable from the tables.
results: GROKE reaches SR 66.4% / NE 56.8 m on TestSet_A and SR 63.3% / NE 59.8 m on TestSet_B. The strongest baseline, a rule-based heuristic agent, gets SR about 18% and NE about 173-181 m. Agent metrics correlate modestly with human navigability judgments (NE r=-0.31, SR r=0.29, n=100).
limitations: Vision-free, so it cannot judge instructions that depend on visual cues absent from OSM (e.g., 'house with red door').
High cost and latency: about 44k tokens per episode with Gemini-3 Pro. Only one LLM was tested, so the JSON-vs-grid finding may not generalize.
Correlation with human judgment is only moderate (|r|≈0.3, n=100), and the ablations use small samples (100 instances, 13 hard).
